newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan proposes annual summits with German leader.
newsitem.headline: Japan proposes annual summits with German leader.

text.p: Japan aims to upgrade ties with Germany and to seal an agreement to hold annual bilateral summit meetings when German Chancellor Helmut Kohl visits Tokyo this week, Japanese Foreign Ministry officials said on Monday.
"We must upgrade our political ties," a Foreign Ministry official in charge of the ministry's German desk told a news briefing.
"Our economic ties have matured, as shown by our two-way trade volume amounting to as much as a fifth of the global total."

Kohl is to arrive in Tokyo on Thursday for a three-day visit. After talks with Emperor Akihito and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Kohl is to speak at a news conference on Friday before leaving on Saturday.

The ministry officials said that apart from brief bilateral sessions during the Group of Seven (G7) summits of the industrialised countries, Japan currently only holds scheduled annual two-way summit meetings with the United States.

"By holding such exclusive meetings every year, we can help Germany look more towards Asia, and we could also discuss common strategy in areas such as regional security in the Middle East and Asia-Pacific," the ministry official said.
Kohl's last visit to Japan was in 1993. Hashimoto has met him twice as prime minister, once during the Asia-Europe ASEM summit in Bangkok in March and at the G7 summit in Lyon, France, in July.
Germany and Japan both aspire to permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council, a topic which may come up in Kohl's talks with Hashimoto, the officials said.
Other issues to be discussed during Kohl's Tokyo visit include possible Japanese aid for unspecified businesses and schools in the former East German provinces, the officials said.
"One area we can readily contribute to is tourism in eastern Germany," he said. "Japanese tourists are not aware of great sites in this part of the country."
